rationale: Phenotypic delineation of Cornelia de Lange syndrome 7 (CDLS7, OMIM #621570) caused by heterozygous MAU2 variants across the Parenti et al. cohort of 18 individuals demonstrates that congenital heart defects are uncommon. The OMIM clinical synopsis based on Parenti et al. documents structural heart defects (specifically atrial septal defect) in only 1 individual (1/18, ~5.6%), well below the 25% threshold (<5 of 18). This contrasts sharply with cohesinopathy cohorts documented in CdLS literature where congenital heart disease affects approximately 34.9% of CdLS patients overall, up to 60% of HDAC8-positive individuals, and ~33-35% of classical NIPBL-positive patients.

evidence.text: In the OMIM entry for Cornelia de Lange syndrome 7 (CDLS7; OMIM #621570) summarizing findings from Parenti et al., the cardiovascular involvement lists atrial septal defect in only 1 individual, indicating an extremely low prevalence of structural congenital heart defects in the cohort.

new_directions.question_text: What is the systematic echocardiographic prevalence of structural and subclinical cardiac defects across an international prospective registry of MAU2 probands?
new_directions.rationale: While ASD was cataloged in only 1 of 18 probands in initial summaries, comprehensive registry reporting with standardized echocardiographic protocols across all individuals is needed to rule out underascertainment of milder cardiac anomalies.

new_directions.question_text: Do truncating MAU2 variants (haploinsufficiency) produce a significantly higher rate of visceral or cardiac malformations compared to in-frame missense variants that primarily impair NIPBL dimerization?
new_directions.rationale: Parenti et al. identified distinct molecular episignatures and functional mechanisms depending on variant type, which could translate into genotype-specific risks for structural malformations.
